blocks.text: Tsawwassen Farms: what the ground is and what governs it

items.t: Hobby acreage vs working-farm ground: no specific farm operation is named on an official source, so the hobby-vs-working split for any single fringe parcel is not confirmed until its use and farm-class record are read. Farm classification matters to value: a parcel that keeps BC Assessment farm classification must keep meeting the minimum gross farm income thresholds, which scale with the size of the operation.

Typical buyer (characterization, not a sourced statistic): working farmers in the Delta belt, hobby-farm and horse buyers on the smaller acreages, and buyers who want ALR land within reach of Tsawwassen and Ladner services.

Municipality and plan: City of Delta. Tsawwassen is one of Delta's three communities (Ladner, Tsawwassen and North Delta), planned under the Delta Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 8400 (2024) — the current OCP consolidated the former area plans (the Tsawwassen Area Plan was Schedule D.1 under the previous OCP, Bylaw No. 3950) into a single Land Use Plan, and its Agriculture policies (OCP s. 2.6, informed by the City's 2023 Agricultural Plan) apply to Delta's agricultural land.
Treaty-land boundary: Tsawwassen First Nation Lands sit on Tsawwassen's western edge. TFN land follows TFN law, not City bylaws.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers

items.t: Zoning number CONTESTED: In the A1 zone the bylaw provides one farm house per lot, a farm house maximum of 500 m², a farm home plate maximum of 3,600 m², one secondary suite inside the farm house, and one accessory farm dwelling unit of maximum 90 m² on lots of 40 ha or less or 186 m² on lots over 40 ha.

Subdivision of farm land (Delta zones): in the A1 zone (s. 10.10.8), subdivision is permitted only where it complies with the Official Community Plan Bylaw and has been approved under the Agricultural Land Commission Act if applicable, and the minimum lot size that may be created by subdivision is 8 ha, with a home site severance exception under Agricultural Land Commission policy; A2 (s. 10.20.6) also sets an 8 ha minimum, and A3 (s. 10.30.6) does not permit subdivision.

Water: the provincial GWELLS application is the registry for recorded wells and aquifers; well reports must be submitted within 90 days after a well is constructed, altered or decommissioned, and older wells may not appear in the registry; under the Water Sustainability Act, domestic groundwater use does not need a licence, and non-domestic use, including irrigation, requires a water licence.

Flood, dykes and foreshore: the City of Delta is the diking authority and operates and maintains over 63 kilometres of flood protection infrastructure, 31 drainage pump stations and approximately 538 kilometres of drainage infrastructure; the City is raising sections of the Boundary Bay dike between 72 Street and 88 Street with provincial grant funding.

The fringe is two different rulebooks stitched together: The same drive from Tsawwassen toward Ladner crosses Agriculture (A)-designated Delta parcels governed by OCP 8400 and — where a parcel is in the ALR — the ALC's housing, subdivision and no-stratification rules layered on top; the parcel-level ALC map check is what tells a buyer which layers apply, and no sub-area label does that work.

Farm ditches trigger an urban-sounding permit area: Every Delta property within 30 m of a stream, slough or ditch — including a working farm's drainage ditch — falls in the Streamside Protection and Enhancement Development Permit Area, so a setback check that buyers associate with city lots applies in the middle of working farm land.

The plan-citation trap is already mapped for this ground: The Tsawwassen Area Plan was Schedule D.1 under the PREVIOUS OCP, Bylaw No. 3950; the current OCP, Bylaw No. 8400 (2024), has NO lettered schedules and designates farm land "Agriculture (A)". Any page or listing attributing a "Schedule D.1 of Bylaw 8400" to Tsawwassen farm land is repeating the conflation error.

The Delta zoning bylaw number is CONTESTED (7600, 2017 vs "8400, 2025") and DSSS Bylaw 8288 (2024) adoption is held not confirmed — while the tsawwassen-east-guide land home asserts 8288 in governing terms. ( disk-checked as the guide land home for that ground.)

Sellers hold the diligence a farm buyer prices first: Document the farm income history that supports the classification and any water licences or ALC approvals in place — those are the items a farm buyer's lender and lawyer will ask for first, and in a thin-information farm sale they are the difference between a financeable parcel and a stalled one.

faq.a: On ALR land, one additional residence is permitted without an ALC application where the conditions are met — 90 m² or less on parcels of 40 ha or smaller, 186 m² or less on larger parcels — and Delta bylaws must also permit it; the A1 zone allows one accessory farm dwelling unit within those same size limits, and a secondary suite is permitted only inside the principal residence.
faq.q: Can a Tsawwassen-area farm have a second dwelling?

faq.a: Water is a diligence item, not an assumption: search GWELLS for the well record (older wells may not appear), and if the operation irrigates, confirm the water licence position — non-domestic groundwater use, including irrigation, requires a licence under the Water Sustainability Act, while domestic groundwater use does not need a licence.
faq.q: Can I irrigate — what water diligence applies?

faq.a: Southlands-side parcels can sit in hazard DPA SD3 (2.9 m floor level, 2.3 m minimum land surface elevation, 7.5 m tidal setback), and any lot within 30 m of a ditch or slough is in the Streamside Protection and Enhancement DPA — farm ditches count. Confirm both with the City, not from a listing's wording.
faq.q: What do the dike and ditch rules mean for a Southlands-side parcel?

faq.a: Both. Delta's Official Community Plan designates farm land on the Tsawwassen edges Agriculture (A) (Bylaw No. 8400, 2024, s. 1.5.1), and Agricultural Land Reserve rules apply where land is in the ALR; the urban neighbourhoods are residential, and the farm topic is that agricultural fringe plus the shared Delta farm belt toward Ladner.
faq.q: Is there real farmland in Tsawwassen, or is it all residential?
